newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to act against calls to boycott poll.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to act against calls to boycott poll.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto said on Thursday authorities would take action against people who encouraged others not to vote in the May 29 general election, the official Antara news agency reported.
"It's their right to be 'White Group'. But they have to stay away. If they try to prevent other people from exercising their rights, we will take action," Suharto said, without elaborating.
The term "White Group" is used to describe Indonesians who abstain from voting or spoil their ballots at the general elections as a protest against government policies.

Indonesia has a colour-coded party system with gold for the ruling Golkar, green representing the Moslem-orientated United Development Party (PPP) and red for the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).
Suharto said the government would also deal harshly with attempts to disrupt the counting of the ballots.
"There will be no compromise," Suharto was quoted as saying while talking with members of a village improvement organisation in Aceh province.
Armed forces commander General Feisal Tanjung had said on Monday authorities would deal harshly with people who attempted to disrupt the elections.
The military in West Java is searching for the people who produced some 6,000 pamphlets calling for a boycott of the poll. About 200 pamphlets were believed to have been distributed.
Members of the unrecognised left-wing People's Democratic Party (PRD) this month started a grafitti campaign calling for a similar boycott.
Most of the leaders of the small group, which went underground last year after being blamed for July riots in Jakarta, are on trial for subversion, which carries a maximum penalty of death.
Golkar, PPP and the PDI are the only three political parties allowed to nominate candidates for elections in Indonesia.
